title: Making Arrangements
goal: Find a time that works, confirm the important details, and change an arrangement when necessary.

study.title: Move from an idea to a plan

can identify a deadline rather than a starting time.

runs.text: If a numerical date could be interpreted in more than one way, spell out the month or ask
For an online meeting across locations,
can prevent a misunderstanding. You do not have to calculate a conversion in your head; confirm what time the meeting is for each person.
can also need clarification when people interpret it differently.
Do you mean Friday the tenth?
checks the actual date rather than relying on the phrase alone.

Thursday doesn't work for me. How about Saturday?
I'm running about ten minutes late.
I can't make it tonight. I'm sorry.
I'll check and let you know tomorrow.

runs.text: I'm running about ten minutes late. Can you wait?

turns.en: I'm running about ten minutes late. Can you wait?

turns.speaker: Drew

runs.text: I can wait until six thirty.

turns.en: I can wait until six thirty.

runs.text: Thanks. I expect to be there by then.

turns.en: Okay. Let me know if that changes.

runs.text: marks an estimate. The other person may have a limit; do not assume everyone can wait indefinitely. A cancellation can be complete without an alternative. Offer a new day if you want to reschedule.
Use this fictional availability table. The café is available from 4 to 9 p.m. in this scene.
Find a time for a thirty-minute café visit on Tuesday. Suggest it, accept it as the friend, and confirm time and place. Support:
Your friend proposes Wednesday. Decline that day and offer a Friday time that fits both schedules.
You have agreed on Friday at 7:15 p.m. Change the response: your friend now needs to finish by 7:30. Either shorten the visit or propose a different plan. Support:
We could meet for fifteen minutes
Send a short text saying you expect to arrive ten minutes late. Rehearse a reply from someone who can wait, then from someone who cannot. Support:
I need to leave at seven thirty
Hide the table. Make a new arrangement using invented availability. Confirm day or date, time, place and whether the answer is definite.
Does six fifteen Tuesday work? — Yes. — Great. Tuesday at six fifteen p.m., at the café.
Wednesday doesn't work for me. Could we meet Friday at seven fifteen? — That works.
We could meet for fifteen minutes
Let's choose another day when we have more time
I'm running about ten minutes late. Can you wait? — I need to leave at seven thirty. — Okay. Let's reschedule.
Is there an actual overlap in availability? Did the final confirmation reflect changes made during the conversation? Could someone follow the plan without guessing the time zone, date or location?

note: 提案だけでは予定は確定しません。相手の返事、日時、待ち合わせ場所をそろえ、変更したときももう一度確認します。
